objects.description: In-memory file buffer: pointer to bytes and their length, used as the basic input for diff/merge. Ownership and lifetime are managed by the caller; library functions read from it.
Generic mutable memory buffer (pointer and size). Used for output of operations like merge results. Caller manages allocation and deallocation.

Parameters for the xdiff preprocessor/diff algorithm. Flags control whitespace/case/algorithm choices; anchors optionally provide line tokens to align on. Caller initializes fields before passing to xdl_diff/xdl_merge.

Callback vtable for emitting diff output. The library calls out_hunk for hunk headers and out_line for individual lines, passing user-provided priv. The user must implement these to collect/print diffs.

Merge parameters: embeds xpp diff params and controls conflict marker size, merge aggressiveness (level), favoring policy, output style, and labels for the three sides.

functions.name: xdl_mmfile_first
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the beginning of the memory buffer represented by the mmfile_t and outputs its size via the size parameter. Intended to expose the raw contents of an in-memory file abstraction for diff/merge operations or for direct inspection.
requirements: mmf must point to an initialized mmfile_t whose ptr references a readable memory block of at least mmf->size bytes and whose size field reflects its length (in bytes).
size is expected to be a valid writable pointer where the function can store the buffer length; whether NULL is permitted is unknown (not documented).
The returned pointer aliases mmf->ptr; ownership and lifetime are controlled by the caller—no transfer of ownership occurs (inferred from struct and signature).
Thread-safety and reentrancy guarantees are unknown.

functions.name: xdl_mmfile_size
functions.description: Returns the size, in bytes, of the buffer represented by the provided mmfile_t. Useful for quickly querying the length of the in-memory file used by the diff/merge routines.
requirements: mmf must point to an initialized mmfile_t; behavior if mmf is NULL is unknown.
The size is returned as a signed long; callers should handle potential large sizes appropriately.

functions.name: xdl_diff
functions.signature: int xdl_diff(mmfile_t *mf1, mmfile_t *mf2, xpparam_t const *xpp, xdemitconf_t const *xecfg, xdemitcb_t *ecb);
functions.description: Computes a textual difference between two in-memory files (mf1 vs mf2) using options in xpp and emission configuration in xecfg, and emits results through the callbacks in ecb. Designed to be called with buffers containing the full contents to diff and caller-provided callbacks to receive hunks and/or lines.
requirements: mf1 and mf2 must each point to initialized mmfile_t objects whose ptr fields reference readable memory blocks of their respective size fields.

xpp may be NULL or non-NULL; specific required flags or constraints are not documented; if provided, flags should be set using XDF_* macros and anchors fields, if used, should be consistent (inferred from types and macros).

xecfg may be NULL or non-NULL; if provided, its fields (ctxlen, interhunkctxlen, flags, find_func, hunk_func) must be initialized to intended values; whether find_func and hunk_func may be NULL is unknown.
ecb must point to an xdemitcb_t prepared for output; whether out_hunk and out_line must be non-NULL, and expected return conventions for these callbacks, are not documented in this header (unknown).
Return value semantics (0/negative/positive) are not documented in this header (unknown).
Thread-safety, performance characteristics, and memory ownership of emitted buffers in out_line are not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: xdl_merge
functions.signature: int xdl_merge(mmfile_t *orig, mmfile_t *mf1, mmfile_t *mf2, xmparam_t const *xmp, mmbuffer_t *result);
functions.description: Performs a three-way merge of mf1 and mf2 with respect to a common ancestor orig, producing the merged result in the supplied mmbuffer_t. Behavior can be tuned via xmparam_t (e.g., conflict markers, merge favor, and style).
requirements: orig, mf1, and mf2 must each point to initialized mmfile_t objects whose ptr fields reference readable memory blocks of their respective size fields.

xmp must point to an initialized xmparam_t containing desired merge parameters (xpp flags, marker_size, level, favor, style, and optional labels); exact valid ranges and semantics for level, favor, and style are indicated by macros in the header but detailed requirements are not documented here.

result must be a valid, writable mmbuffer_t pointer; the function will write the merged data pointer and size; ownership/lifetime of the output buffer and whether the caller must free it are not specified in this header (unknown).
Return value semantics (success/failure codes) are not documented in this header (unknown).
Thread-safety and handling of conflict markers are not documented here (unknown).

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator targets inputs consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR in stubs for:
# - xdl_mmfile_first/xdl_mmfile_size: need non-empty arbitrary bytes
# - xdl_diff: two text buffers; interesting cases include different newlines, tabs, whitespace-only lines,
#   long lines, repeated anchors-like tokens, UTF-8, binary NULs, and mixed encodings
# - xdl_merge: three related versions (orig, mf1, mf2) where conflicts or clean merges can occur
# The framework pulls multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR values per invocation, all sourced from the same seed buffer.
# Therefore, we pack several logically separated payloads in one bytes blob, delimited so the harness can
# split them deterministically (it typically slices sequentially). We avoid malformed data while keeping
# them valid non-empty.
#
# Format we emit (simple concatenation of sections):
#  [section0]\n\n===SEP===\n\n[section1]\n\n===SEP===\n\n[section2]\n\n===SEP===\n\n[section3]\n\n===SEP===\n\n[labels]\n# Sections are:
# 0: Generic text with varied whitespace, different EOLs, tabs, trailing spaces.
# 1: Variant of section0 with small edits: insertions/deletions/moves to exercise diff.
# 2: "orig" for merge base; 1 and 2 (below) will be mf1/mf2 derived from this.
# 3: Second variant for diff and for merge (mf2).
# labels: short C-string-like labels for xdl_merge naming. Not required by FUZZ_PARAM_STR but may be consumed.
# Total size kept <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
SEP = b"\n\n===SEP===\n\n"

def _rand_lines(rng: random.Random, min_lines: int, max_lines: int) -> List[str]:
    n = rng.randint(min_lines, max_lines)
    lines: List[str] = []
    for i in range(n):
        kind = rng.randrange(8)
        if kind == 0:
            # code-like
            name = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 12)))
            val = rng.randint(0, 1000)
            line = f"int {name} = {val};"
        elif kind == 1:
            # function header like
            fn = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 10)))
            args = ', '.join('int ' + ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(1,3)) for _ in range(rng.randint(0,3)))
            line = f"void {fn}({args}) {{"
        elif kind == 2:
            # comment and trailing spaces
            msg = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + ' ') for _ in range(rng.randint(5, 25)))
            line = "// " + msg.rstrip() + (" " * rng.randint(0, 8))
        elif kind == 3:
            # whitespace only
            line = "\t" * rng.randint(0, 3) + " " * rng.randint(0, 8)
        elif kind == 4:
            # long line
            chunk = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + ' _-') for _ in range(rng.randint(40, 120)))
            line = chunk
        elif kind == 5:
            # anchor-like tokens (to interact with anchors feature if enabled)
            token = rng.choice(["TODO", "FIXME", "ANCHOR", "SECTION", "BEGIN", "END"])
            line = f"// {token}: note"
        elif kind == 6:
            # UTF-8 content
            samples = ["αβγ", "Привет", "こんにちは", "مرحبا", "ñandú", "😊"]
            line = rng.choice(samples)
        else:
            # tab-separated values
            cols = ["col" + str(i) for i in range(rng.randint(2, 6))]
            line = "\t".join(cols)
        lines.append(line)
        # occasionally close braces
        if kind == 1 and rng.random() < 0.5:
            lines.append("}")
    return lines

def _apply_newlines(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> bytes:
    # Mix of LF/CRLF/CR
    lines = s.split("\n")
    out: bytearray = bytearray()
    for i, ln in enumerate(lines):
        out.extend(ln.encode('utf-8', errors='surrogatepass'))
        nl_kind = rng.randrange(3)
        if i != len(lines) - 1:
            if nl_kind == 0:
                out.extend(b"\n")
            elif nl_kind == 1:
                out.extend(b"\r\n")
            else:
                out.extend(b"\r")
    return bytes(out)

def _mutate_variant(rng: random.Random, base: List[str]) -> List[str]:
    lines = base[:]
    # perform a few deterministic edits
    edits = rng.randint(3, max(3, len(lines)//4 + 1))
    for _ in range(edits):
        if not lines or rng.random() < 0.2:
            # insertion
            ins = _rand_lines(rng, 1, 2)
            pos = rng.randint(0, len(lines))
            lines[pos:pos] = ins
        else:
            op = rng.randrange(3)
            idx = rng.randrange(len(lines))
            if op == 0:
                # replace
                lines[idx:idx+1] = _rand_lines(rng, 1, 1)
            elif op == 1 and len(lines) > 1:
                # delete
                del lines[idx]
            else:
                # modify whitespace
                lines[idx] = lines[idx] + (" " * rng.randint(0, 4))
    return lines

def _inject_binary(rng: random.Random, data: bytes, ratio: float = 0.02) -> bytes:
    # Introduce a few NULs and random bytes to exercise binary-safe paths while keeping validity
    if not data:
        return data
    ba = bytearray(data)
    count = min(10, max(1, int(len(ba) * ratio)))
    for _ in range(count):
        pos = rng.randrange(len(ba))
        ba[pos] = rng.randrange(256)
    return bytes(ba)

def _mk_labels(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    labs = []
    for prefix in ("BASE", "LEFT", "RIGHT"):
        tail = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(1,6)))
        labs.append(f"{prefix}-{tail}")
    # Join with newlines to provide three separate short tokens
    return ("\n".join(labs)).encode('utf-8')

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Base lines and variants for diff/merge
    base_lines = _rand_lines(rng, 8, 40)
    var1_lines = _mutate_variant(rng, base_lines)
    var2_lines = _mutate_variant(rng, base_lines)

    # Compose sections
    base_text = "\n".join(base_lines)
    var1_text = "\n".join(var1_lines)
    var2_text = "\n".join(var2_lines)

    sec0 = _apply_newlines(rng, base_text)
    sec1 = _apply_newlines(rng, var1_text)
    sec3 = _apply_newlines(rng, var2_text)

    # For merge, orig should be close to base; we use sec0 (textual), optionally tweak slightly
    merge_orig_lines = _mutate_variant(rng, base_lines) if rng.random() < 0.3 else base_lines
    merge_orig_text = "\n".join(merge_orig_lines)
    sec2 = _apply_newlines(rng, merge_orig_text)

    # Light binary injection to cover NUL-safe behavior without breaking overall validity
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        sec0 = _inject_binary(rng, sec0, 0.005)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        sec1 = _inject_binary(rng, sec1, 0.005)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        sec2 = _inject_binary(rng, sec2, 0.003)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        sec3 = _inject_binary(rng, sec3, 0.005)

    labels = _mk_labels(rng)

    parts = [sec0, sec1, sec2, sec3, labels]

    # Ensure non-empty parts (stubs bail on empty strings)
    parts = [p if p else b"\n" for p in parts]

    out = SEP.join(parts)

    # Enforce max total size
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
        # reduce by trimming sections proportionally
        budget = MAX_TOTAL
        per = budget // len(parts) - len(SEP)
        trimmed: List[bytes] = []
        for p in parts:
            if len(p) <= per:
                trimmed.append(p)
            else:
                trimmed.append(p[:max(1, per)])
        out = SEP.join(trimmed)
        out = out[:MAX_TOTAL]

    # Guarantee at least one byte
    if not out:
        out = b"\n"
    return out

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid buffers for fuzz stubs that consume short text labels
# and in-memory file contents for xdl_merge/xmparam/xpparam. The fuzzer will request
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR for:
# - three mmfile contents (orig, mf1, mf2)
# - three labels (ancestor, file1, file2)
# It may also request small anchor tokens in xpparam_t stub.
# We therefore craft a single bytes blob that concatenates multiple newline-separated
# text blocks so that each FUZZ_PARAM_STR can slice a meaningful string. Newlines are
# ideal because xdiff operates line-wise and merges/diffs on line boundaries.
#
# Layout of the generated buffer (all UTF-8 text):
#   Section 1: ancestor/orig file content
#   Section 2: file1 content (variation against ancestor)
#   Section 3: file2 content (different variation against ancestor)
#   Section 4: label ancestor (<=64 chars)
#   Section 5: label file1 (<=64 chars)
#   Section 6: label file2 (<=64 chars)
#   Section 7: optional anchor tokens (0..3 lines, short words)
# Sections are separated by double newlines. Each content section ends with a trailing newline
# to ensure last line is recognized as a full line by diff engines.
#
# The contents include a variety of line styles to exercise behaviors: identical lines,
# modified lines, insertions, deletions, whitespace-only changes, long lines, empty lines,
# and repeated blocks to enable anchors. Sizes remain within the stub limits (< 2048 each,
# total < 4096).

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

LANG_WORDS = [
    "alpha", "beta", "gamma", "delta", "epsilon", "zeta", "theta", "kappa",
    "lambda", "omega", "foo", "bar", "baz", "qux", "quux", "corge",
    "grault", "garply", "waldo", "fred", "plugh", "xyzzy", "thud",
]

FILE_HEADERS = [
    "#include <stdio.h>",
    "// sample configuration",
    "# this is a script",
    "; ini header",
]

LICENSE_SNIPPETS = [
    "// Copyright (c) Example Corp",
    "// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT",
    "/* Licensed under Apache-2.0 */",
]


def _rand_word(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        # mixed alnum token
        length = rng.randint(3, 10)
        chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-"
        return ''.join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(length))
    return rng.choice(LANG_WORDS)


def _gen_label(rng: random.Random, prefix: str) -> str:
    # Generate short label <= 64 chars, ASCII, no nulls.
    parts = [prefix]
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(_rand_word(rng))
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        parts.append(str(rng.randint(1, 99)))
    label = '-'.join(parts)
    # occasionally include path-like flavors
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        label = f"{_rand_word(rng)}/{label}.txt"
    return label[:64]


def _gen_block(rng: random.Random, topic: str, lines: int) -> List[str]:
    out = []
    # optional header
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        out.append(rng.choice(FILE_HEADERS))
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        out.extend(rng.sample(LICENSE_SNIPPETS, k=1))
    # body lines
    for i in range(lines):
        style = rng.random()
        if style < 0.1:
            out.append("")  # empty line
        elif style < 0.2:
            out.append("    ")  # whitespace-only line
        elif style < 0.35:
            # key=value
            key = _rand_word(rng)
            val = _rand_word(rng)
            out.append(f"{key}={val}")
        elif style < 0.55:
            # code-like
            var = _rand_word(rng)
            val = rng.randint(0, 1000)
            out.append(f"int {var} = {val};")
        elif style < 0.75:
            # sentence-like
            words = ' '.join(_rand_word(rng) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)))
            out.append(f"{topic}: {words}.")
        else:
            # long line
            words = '-'.join(_rand_word(rng) for _ in range(rng.randint(8, 16)))
            out.append(words)
    # optional footer marker
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        out.append(f"// end of {topic}")
    return out


def _mutate_lines_for_branch(rng: random.Random, base: List[str]) -> List[str]:
    # Create a variation with insertions, deletions, modifications.
    lines = base[:]
    n = len(lines)
    # Modify some lines (content change)
    for _ in range(max(1, n // 8)):
        idx = rng.randrange(len(lines)) if lines else 0
        if not lines:
            break
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.33 and lines[idx]:
            # subtle whitespace change
            if lines[idx].endswith(' '):
                lines[idx] = lines[idx].rstrip()
            else:
                lines[idx] = lines[idx] + ' '
        elif choice < 0.66:
            # replace with new sentence
            words = ' '.join(_rand_word(rng) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 7)))
            lines[idx] = f"mod: {words}"
        else:
            # change number token if present
            s = lines[idx]
            digits = [i for i, c in enumerate(s) if c.isdigit()]
            if digits:
                i = rng.choice(digits)
                new_digit = str(rng.randint(0, 9))
                lines[idx] = s[:i] + new_digit + s[i+1:]
    # Insert a few lines
    for _ in range(max(1, n // 10)):
        pos = rng.randrange(len(lines)+1)
        lines.insert(pos, f"insert:{_rand_word(rng)}")
    # Delete a few lines (if enough)
    for _ in range(max(1, n // 12)):
        if not lines:
            break
        pos = rng.randrange(len(lines))
        lines.pop(pos)
    return lines


def _ensure_size_limit(sections: List[str], limit: int) -> List[str]:
    total = sum(len(s) for s in sections)
    if total <= limit:
        return sections
    # Trim from the longest content sections conservatively
    trimmed = []
    for s in sections:
        if len(s) > 512 and total > limit:
            new_len = max(128, int(len(s) * 0.7))
            total -= (len(s) - new_len)
            trimmed.append(s[:new_len])
        else:
            trimmed.append(s)
    # If still too large, hard cut the largest piece
    while sum(len(s) for s in trimmed) > limit:
        idx = max(range(len(trimmed)), key=lambda i: len(trimmed[i]))
        trimmed[idx] = trimmed[idx][:max(64, len(trimmed[idx]) - 128)]
    return trimmed


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Create base ancestor content
    base_lines = _gen_block(rng, topic="ancestor", lines=rng.randint(12, 40))
    # Branch variations
    lines1 = _mutate_lines_for_branch(rng, base_lines)
    lines2 = _mutate_lines_for_branch(rng, base_lines)

    # Join with newlines and ensure trailing newline
    def join_lines(ls: List[str]) -> str:
        text = "\n".join(ls)
        if not text.endswith("\n"):
            text += "\n"
        return text

    s_orig = join_lines(base_lines)
    s_f1 = join_lines(lines1)
    s_f2 = join_lines(lines2)

    # Labels (<=64 chars)
    lab_o = _gen_label(rng, "ancestor")
    lab_1 = _gen_label(rng, "ours")
    lab_2 = _gen_label(rng, "theirs")

    # Optional anchors (0..3), each short token
    anchors = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        anchors.append(_rand_word(rng))

    # Compose sections separated by blank lines to let the fuzzer slice distinct FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    sections = [s_orig, s_f1, s_f2, lab_o + "\n", lab_1 + "\n", lab_2 + "\n", "\n".join(anchors) + ("\n" if anchors else "")]

    # Enforce total size cap
    body = "\n\n".join(_ensure_size_limit(sections, MAX_TOTAL - 32))

    # Final safety: ensure under hard cap
    data = body.encode('utf-8')[:MAX_TOTAL]
    return data
